title: How condo buyers review resale certificates fast: a Mac guide for realtors
metaTitle: Condo Buyers Review Resale Certificates on a Tight Clock
description: Tight HOA review windows squeeze condo buyers. See the timelines, costs, and fixes realtors can use on a Mac, with Lazur for the rest.
intro: Condo buyers review resale certificates inside a window that state law and the purchase contract set. In many places that window is short, and the HOA package often arrives close to the deadline. This page covers why the squeeze happens, what it costs you, and what you can fix this week with tools already on your Mac.
tldr: The HOA usually has 5 to 10 business days to deliver the resale package, and the order often goes out 30 to 60 days before escrow.
Review windows differ by state. Florida gives condo buyers 7 days, excluding weekends and legal holidays, while California sets no separate review period for HOA documents.
Order the package early, put the deadline in your calendar the day it arrives, and triage with the warning signs before you read every page.
Treat the first pass as a screen. One vendor estimates a basic screen at about 90 minutes, and a full packet can run to hundreds of pages.

blocks.text: Why the resale package arrives late

Most condo buyers do not get the resale package at the start of the deal. The package is a set of HOA documents for the sale. It can include the CC&Rs, bylaws, rules, budget, reserve study, and board meeting minutes. Someone has to order it, and the HOA has to deliver it. That is where the timing goes wrong.

Practitioner guidance from Associa says an HOA usually has 5 to 10 business days to provide the resale package. The buyer's agent or title company typically orders it, and the order goes out 30 to 60 days before escrow. If that order goes out late, the package lands near the end of escrow. The buyer then reviews a long packet on a short clock.
The timeline that breaks a tight window

items: Offer accepted. The contract sets the escrow timeline, and the clock is already running.
Order placed. The buyer's agent or title company asks the HOA manager for the package.
HOA works on it. Expect 5 to 10 business days, and add time for holidays.
Package arrives. Your review window starts, or part of it is already gone.
Deadline. The buyer decides whether to cancel, close, or ask for more time.

blocks.text: Each step is ordinary on its own. The problem is the total. A package ordered late, delivered slowly, and reviewed on a short clock leaves the buyer very little room. Map your own deals against this list before the next offer. You will see which step is the slow one.
How long the review window is in your state

There is no single national rule for this. GoverningDocs reports state review windows that range from 3 to 10 days. Some states set no statutory period at all. The examples below come from secondary sources, so confirm each one against the current statute before you rely on it.

rows: Buyer may cancel within 7 days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays
10 business days to deliver the resale certificate. The buyer cancel right varies by source.
Statute text could not be opened, so verify
Delivery within 10 days of a written request. No separate review period.
10 days to deliver. Cancel right until midnight of the 5th calendar day after receipt.
blocks.caption: Examples from secondary sources. Verify each one before you rely on it.

blocks.text: California shows why you should read the statute yourself. GoverningDocs says HOA documents must be delivered within 10 days of a written request under Civil Code 4530. It also says California sets no separate review period for them. The 3-day right in Civil Code 1102.3 covers the seller's transfer disclosure, not the HOA package.
Florida's 7-day rule, worked through

Florida is the clearest recent change. HB 913 extended the condo cancel right from 3 days to 7 days for sales by nondeveloper unit owners. The change took effect July 1, 2025. The statute excludes Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, and that exclusion changes the math more than most people expect.

Here is a worked example. The package reaches the buyer on a Monday. Start counting on Tuesday, skip Saturday and Sunday, and the seventh counted day lands on the Wednesday of the following week. A legal holiday in that stretch pushes the deadline later. Secondary sources disagree on how to count, so ask the title company to confirm.

blocks.title: Do not count calendar days
blocks.text: Weekend days do not count under Florida's condo rule. A package that arrives on a Friday loses the weekend. The first counted day is Monday, so the deadline moves past the weekend.
Spot the red flags in the first pass

A basic screen is triage, not a full review. GoverningDocs estimates about 90 minutes for a basic screen. It lists the CC&Rs as the largest slice, at 30 minutes. It also says a full package can run to hundreds of pages. Plan for the screen first, then decide what needs a slower read.

items: Reserve funding under 30%. GoverningDocs lists this as an early warning sign.
Components past their useful life, based on the reserve study.
Deferred maintenance mentioned in board minutes.
Vague assessment language that leaves owners unsure what they will pay.

blocks.text: GoverningDocs says these signs often appear months or years before a special assessment. Treat each one as a question for the HOA, not as proof of a problem. Write the question down with the page number, so you can send all of them in one email.
Use Preview and Gmail for a faster first pass

You do not need a paid tool to find these signs. Open the PDF in Preview, then press ⌘F. Search for reserve, special assessment, deferred, and litigation. Preview lists the matches, so you can move from one hit to the next without scrolling the whole packet.

When you find a section that matters, mark it up. Apple's Preview guide says you can highlight, underline, and strike out text. You can also add notes and speech bubbles to a PDF. Use a note to write the page number and your question for the HOA manager.

Keep each building in one folder. Name each PDF with the building and the document type, such as CC&Rs or minutes. In Gmail, search has:attachment filename:pdf to find packets that came by email. Then you attach the right file without digging through your inbox.
Build a tracker in Google Sheets

A spreadsheet beats memory when several deals run at once. Use one row per document. Name the columns Building, Document, Date received, Deadline, Red flags, Question for HOA, and Status. The next deal then starts from the same sheet.

items: Open a sheet in Google Sheets in Chrome, or copy the one you already use.
Enter each deadline as a real date, not as text, so sorting and formatting work.
Select the Deadline column, then open Format > Conditional formatting to shade dates that are close to today.
Copy text from an HOA email and paste it with ⌘⇧V. That pastes values only, so old formatting does not follow the cell.

blocks.text: The sheet does one job. It keeps the deadline visible on the day the package lands. For more on sheet layouts for deal work, read [Google Sheets for realtors on Mac](/for/realtors/google-sheets).
Write the request to the HOA manager

Send the request early and in writing. Name the property, the documents you need, and the date you need them by. Ask for the recent board minutes along with the full package. Minutes often show deferred work and disputes. Keep the email short so the manager can answer it in one pass.

In Gmail, click the arrow next to Send and choose Schedule send if you want the email to go out at a set time. You can also keep a template for this request. The [Gmail guide for realtors](/for/realtors/gmail) covers templates and scheduled sends.
What to put in the contract

Practitioner guidance lists a document review contingency as one way to protect the buyer. A contingency sets a defined path if the package raises concerns. Its effect depends on the wording and your state, so have the language checked before you use it.

Ask your broker or the buyer's attorney what the contract says about late documents. Do not guess at the answer. Follow your brokerage's rules on contract language, and ask the title company before you change a clause.
Privacy and client files

Resale packages carry owner names, addresses, and financial details. Check your brokerage's rules before you share a packet with any AI tool. Lazur only looks at your screen while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Where Lazur helps, and where it does not

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on your screen, and Lazur answers out loud. For a packet, it can point at a section you name, explain a clause in plain words, draft the request, or take dictated notes. Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in any app.

It does not read the whole packet for you. It sees what is on your screen. It does not click buttons or edit your files, and it does not decide whether a building is a good buy. You still read the documents and make the call.

Research jobs run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. Use one to pull up the statute text for your state, then read the statute yourself. The job returns a summary and a report. Check both against the source before you tell a client anything.

blocks.title: Start with the statute
blocks.text: Look up the review window before the package arrives. The window sets the pace for every other step on this page, so put it on the first line of your tracker.

faq.question: How many days do condo buyers have to review resale certificates?
faq.answer: It depends on the state. Florida gives condo buyers 7 days to cancel, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays. Virginia's default is 3 days, and it is negotiable. California sets no separate review period for HOA documents. Check the statute for your state before you rely on any number.

faq.question: Who orders the HOA resale package?
faq.answer: Practitioner guidance says the buyer's agent or title company typically orders it, about 30 to 60 days before escrow. Confirm who owns the order step in your deal, and write the name and date in your tracker.

faq.question: How long does the HOA take to deliver the package?
faq.answer: Practitioner guidance says an HOA usually has 5 to 10 business days to provide the resale package. Add time for holidays. If nothing has arrived by the due date, follow up in writing the same day.

faq.question: Does California's 3-day rule cover HOA documents?
faq.answer: GoverningDocs says no. The 3-day right in Civil Code 1102.3 applies to the seller's transfer disclosure, not to HOA documents. California has no separate statutory review period for the HOA package, so check the contract language.

faq.question: What does a basic HOA document screen cover?
faq.answer: GoverningDocs estimates about 90 minutes for a basic screen. It covers the CC&Rs, reserve study, budget, meeting minutes, bylaws, and rules. It is a first pass, not a full review, and a full packet can run to hundreds of pages.

faq.question: Can Lazur read the whole resale packet for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur sees what is on your screen while you hold the shortcut. It can point at a section, explain it in plain words, and help you draft questions. You still read the documents and decide what they mean for your client.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: No. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. You can start the 3-day Pro trial from the download page, and it needs no credit card. Pricing details are on the pricing page.

costs.title: Time you do not bill
costs.text: Most sales agents are self-employed, so review hours come out of unpaid time. BLS reports that 54% of real estate sales agents were self-employed in 2025. The median annual pay for sales agents was $52,830 in May 2025. A long packet read on a weekend is still your time.

costs.title: A missed cancel window
costs.text: If the window closes before you finish, the buyer may lose the right to cancel. In Florida, that right runs for 7 days, excluding weekends and legal holidays. A slow read can turn into a deal the buyer cannot undo. Plan the read so it finishes before the deadline.

costs.title: Red flags that surface after closing
costs.text: GoverningDocs says low reserves, aging components, and deferred maintenance often appear months or years before a special assessment. A page you skipped can become a bill for the buyer after closing. Your client then remembers who said the building looked fine.

costs.title: Late orders that squeeze every step
costs.text: Associa describes an order placed 30 to 60 days before escrow. An order placed late squeezes every other step. The HOA then needs 5 to 10 business days, and the buyer reads on whatever time is left.

costs.title: Trust that is hard to earn back
costs.text: A buyer who feels rushed stops trusting your advice. A buyer who learns about a red flag after the deadline may blame the timing, and the trust goes with it. Put the review plan in writing from the first day of the deal.

causes.title: HOA packages are common
causes.text: HOAs are part of many homes. In 2023, 64.8% of new single-family homes started were in a community or homeowners association, according to NAHB's reading of Census Survey of Construction data. Many of your buyers will see a package. Your process has to handle one every time, not as a rare case.

causes.title: State windows vary widely
causes.text: Review windows range from 3 to 10 days across states, and some states set no separate period. The same contract can give a buyer a week in one state and no fixed window in another. Your process has to change with the state, not with your memory of the last deal.

causes.title: HOA turnaround is outside your control
causes.text: Practitioner guidance says an HOA usually has 5 to 10 business days to provide the package. You cannot speed up the manager. You can order early and follow up on the due date. Those two steps are what you control.

causes.title: Nobody owns the order step
causes.text: The buyer's agent or title company usually places the order. If nobody owns that step in the deal, it goes out late. The package then lands close to the deadline, which is the squeeze this page describes.

causes.title: Long packets with no triage
causes.text: A full package can run to hundreds of pages, according to GoverningDocs. Reading every page at the same depth wastes time on routine material. Without a triage method, a warning sign can sit deep in the packet with nothing to flag it.

causes.title: One person does the reading
causes.text: Most sales agents are self-employed, according to BLS. That usually means one person reads the package and tracks the deadline. Nobody else catches the page you missed, so the process has to do that job.

fixes.title: Order the package early
fixes.text: Ask the buyer's agent or title company to order the resale package 30 to 60 days before escrow, which is the timing Associa describes. Put the order date on your calendar. An early order gives the HOA time to deliver before the review window gets short. No new tool is needed for this step.

fixes.title: Confirm the window from the statute text
fixes.text: Find your state's review rule in the statute itself. Florida's condo rule sits in Florida Statutes 718.503, and the Florida Legislature site hosts the text for free. For other states, look up the statute number from a trusted secondary source, then read the official text. Note the date you checked it in your tracker.

fixes.title: Read the minutes before the bylaws
fixes.text: Minutes show what the board discussed, including deferred maintenance and disputes. GoverningDocs lists deferred maintenance in board minutes as a warning sign. Start with the minutes, then decide which parts of the CC&Rs need a full read. This order saves time on a tight clock.

fixes.title: Triage with the warning signs
fixes.text: Check the reserve funding level, component age, deferred work, assessment language, and litigation. Write each finding as a question for the HOA. A short question list is quicker to send than a full review is to finish, and the HOA can answer it in one reply.

fixes.title: Use Preview search on every PDF
fixes.text: Open the PDF in Preview and press ⌘F. Search for reserve, special assessment, deferred, and litigation. Add a note with the page number to each hit. The search takes a short time per packet, and it shows you where to read slowly.

fixes.title: Ask for more time in writing
fixes.text: If the package arrives late, ask the other side for more time in writing. Name the new date and the documents still missing. Keep the request short, and keep the reply in the file. Do not assume the buyer's cancel right moves with the delay until you check the contract and the statute.

fixes.title: Use a document review contingency
fixes.text: Practitioner guidance lists a document review contingency as one way to protect the buyer. Ask your broker or attorney how the wording works in your state before you use it. Clear language sets the review deadline before the package arrives, so everyone works from the same clock.

plan.label: Day 1
plan.title: Confirm the window and order the package
plan.text: Look up your state's review rule and write the statute number in your tracker. Ask the buyer's agent or title company to order the resale package, and note the date you asked.

plan.label: Day 2
plan.title: Build the tracker
plan.text: Open Google Sheets in Chrome and add the columns Building, Document, Date received, Deadline, Red flags, Question for HOA, and Status. Enter the deadline as a real date so the shading works.

plan.label: Morning
plan.title: Triage the packet in Preview
plan.text: Open each PDF, press ⌘F, and search for reserve, special assessment, deferred, and litigation. Add a note with the page number for each hit.

plan.label: Afternoon
plan.title: Read the minutes, then the budget
plan.text: Read the recent minutes for deferred work and disputes. Then open the budget and reserve study. Log each question in the tracker so the HOA gets one email, not five.

plan.label: Final check
plan.title: Send the questions and set the reminder
plan.text: Schedule one email to the HOA manager in Gmail, then set an Apple Reminders item for the deadline. Ask Lazur to add the reminder by voice if that is faster for you.
